From: Office of the Relief Coordinator, Panvel
Date: 11 August 2026, 09:15 IST
Subject: Wind-down of relief operations, accounting of assets, and partner acknowledgements

1. This memo covers the phased closure of the relief operation. The focus of the last ten days has shifted from evacuation and shelter management to return of families, decommissioning of temporary facilities, and reconciliation of all material and financial records. Shelter supervisors are requested to treat this memo as the standing instruction for closure activities until a separate order is issued.

2. Shelter closure sequence. Each shelter will be closed in the order given in the attached Annexure A. The order is based on the condition of the building, the number of families still residing, and the availability of transport for returning families. Shelters with full occupancy will be closed last. The supervisor of each shelter must submit a readiness report to the control room 24 hours before the planned closure of that shelter. The report must state the current family count, the condition of the building, and any pending repairs that were carried out during the occupation period.

3. Return of families. Families are to return to their homes only after the ward volunteer has confirmed that the house is safe for entry. The ward volunteer will coordinate with the village panchayat for this purpose. In areas where water has not fully receded, the ward volunteer will mark the house as unsafe and the family will remain in the shelter until further notice. A register of returned families is to be maintained at each shelter. The register will be collected by the block development officer on the day of shelter closure. Families who require transport assistance for return will be provided a vehicle from the same pool that was used for evacuation. The route plan for return will be the reverse of the evacuation route, except where the road condition has changed. Any change in route will be communicated by the control room in writing.

4. Return of cattle from the temporary camp at Panvel market yard. The Animal Husbandry department has confirmed that the camp will function until 18 August. After that date, the camp will be closed and any unclaimed cattle will be handed over to the nearest gaushala. Owners who have not yet collected their animals are requested to do so before 17 August. The registration slip issued at the time of deposit must be produced at the time of release. In case the slip is lost, the owner must provide a written declaration and a witness from the village panchayat. The Animal Husbandry department has reported that the condition of the cattle at the camp is satisfactory. Two animals were treated for minor injuries, and one calf was born at the camp on 9 August. The calf and the mother are healthy.

5. Accounting of relief material. All relief material, including food packets, water bottles, blankets, tarpaulins, and hygiene kits, is to be counted and recorded in the stock register at each shelter. The closing stock will be transferred to the central store at the Panvel taluka office on the date of shelter closure. The supervisor and the storekeeper will jointly sign the transfer note. Any shortage or damage must be reported immediately with the reason. Consumable items that have crossed their expiry date are to be segregated and handed over to the health department for disposal. Do not mix expired items with the closing stock. The health department has issued a circular on disposal procedure, which is available at the control room.

6. Financial reconciliation. All expenses incurred during the operation are to be entered in the expenditure register with supporting vouchers. The following categories are to be used: transport, food, medicine, communication, repair and maintenance, and miscellaneous. The accountant will visit each shelter on 14 and 15 August to verify the registers. Shelter supervisors are requested to keep all vouchers ready for inspection. Expenses that are not supported by a voucher will not be reimbursed. Petty cash advances given to supervisors must be settled with the accountant before the final closure of the shelter. The advance amount and the settlement amount must match; any difference will be recovered from the supervisor's salary.

**PANVEL COASTAL RELIEF CELL**
Internal Memo Series – Document No. 27
From: Office of the Relief Coordinator, Panvel
Date: 11 August 2026, 09:15 IST
Subject: Wind-down of relief operations, accounting of assets, and partner acknowledgements

1. This memo covers the phased closure of the relief operation. The focus of the last ten days has shifted from evacuation and shelter management to return of families, decommissioning of temporary facilities, and reconciliation of all material and financial records. Shelter supervisors are requested to treat this memo as the standing instruction for closure activities until a separate order is issued.

2. Shelter closure sequence. Each shelter will be closed in the order given in the attached Annexure A. The order is based on the condition of the building, the number of families still residing, and the availability of transport for returning families. Shelters with full occupancy will be closed last. The supervisor of each shelter must submit a readiness report to the control room 24 hours before the planned closure of that shelter. The report must state the current family count, the condition of the building, and any pending repairs that were carried out during the occupation period.

3. Return of families. Families are to return to their homes only after the ward volunteer has confirmed that the house is safe for entry. The ward volunteer will coordinate with the village panchayat for this purpose. In areas where water has not fully receded, the ward volunteer will mark the house as unsafe and the family will remain in the shelter until further notice. A register of returned families is to be maintained at each shelter. The register will be collected by the block development officer on the day of shelter closure. Families who require transport assistance for return will be provided a vehicle from the same pool that was used for evacuation. The route plan for return will be the reverse of the evacuation route, except where the road condition has changed. Any change in route will be communicated by the control room in writing.

4. Return of cattle from the temporary camp at Panvel market yard. The Animal Husbandry department has confirmed that the camp will function until 18 August. After that date, the camp will be closed and any unclaimed cattle will be handed over to the nearest gaushala. Owners who have not yet collected their animals are requested to do so before 17 August. The registration slip issued at the time of deposit must be produced at the time of release. In case the slip is lost, the owner must provide a written declaration and a witness from the village panchayat. The Animal Husbandry department has reported that the condition of the cattle at the camp is satisfactory. Two animals were treated for minor injuries, and one calf was born at the camp on 9 August. The calf and the mother are healthy.

5. Accounting of relief material. All relief material, including food packets, water bottles, blankets, tarpaulins, and hygiene kits, is to be counted and recorded in the stock register at each shelter. The closing stock will be transferred to the central store at the Panvel taluka office on the date of shelter closure. The supervisor and the storekeeper will jointly sign the transfer note. Any shortage or damage must be reported immediately with the reason. Consumable items that have crossed their expiry date are to be segregated and handed over to the health department for disposal. Do not mix expired items with the closing stock. The health department has issued a circular on disposal procedure, which is available at the control room.

6. Financial reconciliation. All expenses incurred during the operation are to be entered in the expenditure register with supporting vouchers. The following categories are to be used: transport, food, medicine, communication, repair and maintenance, and miscellaneous. The accountant will visit each shelter on 14 and 15 August to verify the registers. Shelter supervisors are requested to keep all vouchers ready for inspection. Expenses that are not supported by a voucher will not be reimbursed. Petty cash advances given to supervisors must be settled with the accountant before the final closure of the shelter. The advance amount and the settlement amount must match; any difference will be recovered from the supervisor's salary.

Water level readings are taken from the nearest river/stream gauge or the marked staff gauge at the shelter premises, in meters.
